title: Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 — Section 24 (Effect of Other Laws)

content.overview: Section 24 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 provides that the Act and rules or orders made under it shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any enactment other than the EPA. It also saves actions under other laws that are not inconsistent. Section 24 is the supremacy clause that prevents ordinary inconsistent State or other Central legislation from defeating EPA standards and directions.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Is there inconsistency with another enactment? (2) Does EPA/rule/order prevail under s. 24? (3) Is the other law action consistent and therefore saved?
content.study:
s. 24 does not repeal other environmental statutes; it ensures EPA prevails in case of inconsistency. Water Act and Air Act continue to operate in their fields subject to this rule.

No new case invented.

sections.heading: Non-obstante effect
sections.body: EPA and rules/orders under it prevail notwithstanding anything inconsistent in any other enactment.

sections.heading: Saving
sections.body: Actions under other laws that are not inconsistent with the EPA remain valid as the section provides.

sections.heading: Practical effect
sections.body: Stricter or specific EPA standards and directions are not defeated by inconsistent provisions in other statutes.

sections.heading: Coordination
sections.body: Water Act, Air Act and sector statutes continue; conflict is resolved in favour of EPA where inconsistency is shown.

sections.heading: Method
sections.body: Identify the competing provision; test inconsistency; apply s. 24 precedence if made out.

examples.title: Inconsistent local permission
examples.body: A local permission under another statute allows emission above EPA standards — s. 24 gives effect to the EPA standard notwithstanding the inconsistent permission.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 24 repeal the Water Act?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. s. 24 is a conflict rule; consistent operation of other environmental statutes continues.

distinctions.title: EPA supremacy vs sector statutes
distinctions.left: EPA prevails over inconsistent provisions in other enactments.
distinctions.right: Water/Air Acts remain operative for medium-specific consent where consistent.

misconceptions.trap: EPA replaces all other environmental laws.
misconceptions.correction: s. 24 only resolves inconsistency; it does not wipe out consistent sector regulation.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Non-obstante effect; saving of consistent actions; coordination with sector Acts.
